images.title: The 3 by 3 prime grid
images.purpose: Show the puzzle to solve: an empty 3 by 3 grid with row products 8, 105, 70 and column products 30, 70, 28.
images.composition: One 3 by 3 grid centred with generous margins, row products to its right, column products below.
images.exact_structure: One grid of exactly 9 equal empty square cells (3 rows, 3 columns) with a teal #0072B2 outline. To the right of rows 1, 2, 3 the numbers 8, 105, 70 in amber #E69F00. Below columns 1, 2, 3 the numbers 30, 70, 28 in amber #E69F00. Cells stay empty. Exactly 9 cells, 6 numbers.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any number written inside the grid cells
images.takeaway: Each row and column of primes must multiply to its number.
images.description: An empty 3 by 3 grid with row products 8, 105, 70 on the right and column products 30, 70, 28 below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the row with product 8 and say which primes could multiply to 8.

image_decisions.why: The grid with its six products is the whole puzzle; one clean image carries it.
